proofs.proof_tex:
Fix a full-dimensional connected chamber \(C\) of
\(\mathcal M^{\circ}_{\mathrm{fork},2,4}(G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\).
We first prove the asserted equality of sets.

Let
\(\theta\in\mathcal E_2(G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\cap C\).
By the definition of \(\mathcal E_2\), there is a legal point
\(\theta'\in\mathcal M_{2,4}(G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\) such that
\[
 \Sigma_{\theta'}^{(k)}=\Sigma_{\theta}^{(k)}
 \qquad\text{for every }k\in K.
\]
Because \(\theta\in C\) lies in the stated regular fork locus,
\(\mathrm{thm:fork\text{-}eight\text{-}branch\text{-}classification}\) applies.  Its
completeness direction selects one of the eight factor-line indices
\(\eta\in\{0,1\}^3\) and returns scalars \((s,x)\in\mathbb R^2\) satisfying
the branch's baseline-variance, intervention-variance, denominator,
exact-support, retained-edge, mixing, and exceptional-polynomial conditions.
The same result verifies the five displayed covariance equations.  Hence
\((\theta,s,x)\in\mathscr S_{\eta,C}\), and therefore
\[
 \theta\in
 \bigcup_{\eta\in\{0,1\}^3}\pi_C(\mathscr S_{\eta,C}).
\]

Conversely, suppose that
\(\theta\in\pi_C(\mathscr S_{\eta,C})\) for some \(\eta\).  Then there are
\((s,x)\in\mathbb R^2\) with \((\theta,s,x)\in\mathscr S_{\eta,C}\).
By the soundness direction of
\(\mathrm{thm:fork\text{-}eight\text{-}branch\text{-}classification}\), the
branch solution reconstructs a point
\(\theta'\in\mathcal M_{2,4}(G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\): all four baseline
variances and all four intervention variances are positive, every required
coefficient and change is nonzero, every changed edge is retained, and the
mixing columns are nonzero and pairwise noncollinear.  That theorem's final
calculation gives
\[
 \Sigma_{\theta'}^{(k)}-\Sigma_{\theta'}^{(0)}
 =D_k
 =\Sigma_{\theta}^{(k)}-\Sigma_{\theta}^{(0)}
 \qquad(k\in V),
\]
while its baseline equation gives
\(\Sigma_{\theta'}^{(0)}=\Sigma_{\theta}^{(0)}\).  Adding the baseline
equality to each difference equality proves
\[
 \Sigma_{\theta'}^{(k)}=\Sigma_{\theta}^{(k)}
 \qquad(k\in K).
\]
Thus \(\theta\in\mathcal E_2(G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\cap C\).
The two inclusions prove
\[
 \mathcal E_2(G_{\mathrm{fork}},G'_{\mathrm{fork}})\cap C
 =\bigcup_{\eta\in\{0,1\}^3}\pi_C(\mathscr S_{\eta,C}).
\]

We next translate this equality into the information-frontier criterion.
For an arbitrary subset \(A\subseteq C\), the complement
\(C\setminus\operatorname{cl}_C(A)\) is relatively open in \(C\).  It is
therefore nonempty if and only if its relative interior is nonempty.  Hence
\[
 \operatorname{relint}_C\bigl(C\setminus\operatorname{cl}_C(A)\bigr)
 =\varnothing
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{cl}_C(A)=C.
\]
In words, the displayed relative-interior condition is exactly density in
\(C\).

The fork locus is obtained from the branch locus by deleting the zero sets
of the finitely many additional nonzero polynomials in
\(\mathcal Q_{\mathrm{fork}}\).  For completeness, a nonzero real polynomial
cannot vanish on a nonempty open set: induction on the number of variables
reduces the assertion to the fact that a nonzero univariate polynomial has
only finitely many roots, after viewing the polynomial as a univariate
polynomial whose coefficients are polynomials in the remaining variables.
Consequently each deleted zero set has empty relative interior in every
full-dimensional branch chamber.  The fork locus is thus relatively open
and dense there, and its full-dimensional connected chambers form an open
dense refinement.

If a set is dense in a branch chamber, its intersection with every member
of this open refinement is dense in that member: every nonempty relatively
open subset of the member is also relatively open in the branch chamber.
Conversely, if the intersections are dense in all refining chambers, their
closures contain their union, and the closure of that union is the whole
branch chamber because the refinement is dense.  Therefore the density test
in the definition of \(\mathsf{Cov}_2(G_{\mathrm{fork}})\) is equivalent to
the same test on every chamber \(C\) appearing in the theorem.  By
\(\mathrm{prop:fork\text{-}rational\text{-}collision}\),
\[
 G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\notin
 \mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}(G_{\mathrm{fork}}).
\]
Using the definition
\(\mathsf{Frontier}_2=\mathsf{Cov}_2\setminus\mathsf H_{\mathrm{soft}}\),
the just-proved set equality, and the density equivalence yields
\[
 G'_{\mathrm{fork}}\in\mathsf{Frontier}_2(G_{\mathrm{fork}})
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad
 \operatorname{relint}_C\!\left(
 C\setminus\operatorname{cl}_C
 \left(\bigcup_{\eta\in\{0,1\}^3}
 \pi_C(\mathscr S_{\eta,C})\right)
 \right)=\varnothing
\]
for every full-dimensional connected fork chamber \(C\).

It remains to prove the stated limitation of the worked family.  Its true
coordinates obey fixed affine equalities, including
\[
 v_1=v_2=v_3=v_4=1,
\]
and fixed equalities for the displayed baseline coefficient and loading
coordinates.  Its image is consequently contained in a proper affine
algebraic subset \(Z\) of the full-dimensional true-parameter domain.  Let
\(C\) be a full-dimensional chamber meeting this family.  The relatively
open semialgebraic set \(C\setminus Z\) is nonempty, so it contains a point
\(\theta_0\) and a sufficiently small relative open ball \(B\) whose closure
in \(C\) is disjoint from \(Z\).  Put
\[
 P_0=C\setminus\overline B,
 \qquad
 P_1=C.
\]
Both \(P_0\) and \(P_1\) are relatively semialgebraic.  Since
\(Z\cap\overline B=\varnothing\), both contain the same worked true-coordinate
family and a relative neighborhood of each of its points.  Nevertheless,
\[
 B\subseteq C\setminus\operatorname{cl}_C(P_0),
 \qquad
 C\setminus\operatorname{cl}_C(P_1)=\varnothing.
\]
Because \(B\) is nonempty and relatively open, it follows that
\[
 \operatorname{relint}_C
 \bigl(C\setminus\operatorname{cl}_C(P_0)\bigr)\ne\varnothing,
 \qquad
 \operatorname{relint}_C
 \bigl(C\setminus\operatorname{cl}_C(P_1)\bigr)=\varnothing.
\]
Thus the rational family, even with its audited regular neighborhoods, is
consistent with relatively semialgebraic supersets having opposite density
answers.  It cannot by itself determine the answer for the actual projected
union.  Only a global argument applied to all eight projections can produce
the chamberwise dense realization cover or a full-dimensional separator,
which proves the final assertion.

prose_updates.tldr: Actual soft-intervention rows \(h_k^{\mathsf T}=\delta_k^{\mathsf T}(I_q-\Lambda^{(0)})^{-1}\) admit the proved terminal-copy and affine-support compatibility test. In the noninjective regime \(2\le p<q\), regular covariance twins are exactly a finite union of positive-real factor-line projections. For the \(p=2,q=4\) fork, all eight branches reduce losslessly to two candidate scalars and reconstruct the original five covariance equations. The mandated fixed resultant/subresultant projection attempt with all true coordinates free did not emit projection polynomials or Thom-cell certificates, so the all-chamber density gate failed. The bounded-width item is only a supporting finite-reduction result: its \(\omega_p\) premise is unused, and no compiler, complexity, or pathwidth headline is supported. The prospective LCD workflow may report corrected actual-row compatibility and verified individual covariance twins, but it cannot yet certify whether higher cumulants remove all generic covariance alternatives.

project_justification.gap: Problem 5.2 of Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal asks whether covariance and higher-cumulant information distinguish compatible graph classes. After correcting Definition 3.14 to use actual intervention rows, the noninjective covariance question is the density of a union of positive-real projected branches in every full-dimensional sign-and-variance chamber. The prescribed fork-only Collins--Hong-style projection with \(s\) and \(x\) eliminated and all true coordinates left free failed before producing an explicit projection family, sign-cell refinement, or Thom samples. Thus neither the fork density alternative nor the graph-specific non-quantifier-elimination criterion is established.
project_justification.niche: The proved contribution isolates the exact obstruction. Terminal compatibility has finite linkage and affine certificates, while every regular covariance twin belongs to one of at most \(2^{q-r}\) factor-line systems. The four-node fork is reduced exactly to eight bivariate systems containing every positivity, denominator, support, retention, mixing, and covariance condition. What remains is global projection geometry over all true parameters, not another collision or local Jacobian witness.
project_justification.fill: The paper delivers the corrected terminal algorithm, the exact covariance-branch reduction, the complete regular two-scalar fork reduction, and a positive rational covariance collision checked in all five contexts. It proves the exact projected-union criterion and proves that the rational family together with its audited local neighborhoods cannot decide chamberwise density. The failed full-symbolic projection gate leaves the all-graph compiler as an open-ended question. No bounded-width compiler, certificate-height bound, bit complexity, pathwidth guarantee, all-graph criterion, or infinite generic-strictness family is claimed.

prose_updates.related_work: Leyes Carreno, Meroni, and Seigal (2025) derive the actual intervention-row system in Equation (20), use the observational inverse-path class in Definition 3.14, state recovery through Theorem 1.7, and pose graph and covariance questions in Problems 5.1--5.2. The terminal-copy result repairs the mismatch between the actual rows and the observational-path substitution. Squires, Seigal, Bhate, and Uhler (2023) recover transitive-closure information for injective soft-intervention models; their injective result does not decide the noninjective positive-real covariance projection considered here. Half-trek, semidefinite realization, affine-birational transfer, and tree-accelerated real-elimination work remain methodological context. In particular, a standard resultant/subresultant projection over the complete true-parameter block is not the requested graph-specific criterion, and the failed fork attempt supplies no complexity comparison for a covariance-terminal-width compiler.
prose_updates.interpretation: The corrected compatible graph set is operational at population level once the aligned factor rows are available. Covariance-only alternatives are represented exactly by finite branch systems, and every returned fork candidate can be checked against each of the five original context covariance equations. The positive rational collision proves existence and local robustness, not generic covariance surplus. The single fixed all-parameter elimination attempt produced neither a dense-cover certificate nor a full-dimensional separator. Until the complete projected union is classified, the LCD consumer must report the high-cumulant-versus-covariance distinction as unresolved.
prose_updates.technical_internal_limitation: The mandated early-kill construction used the full twenty-four-coordinate fork support chart \(A,\Lambda^{(0)},\delta,v,t\), retained \(s\) and \(x\) as the only eliminated candidate variables, generated the eight loading-line choices from the exact covariance factors, used a Cramer chart for \(v'=v'_0+sn\), and specified a fixed coefficients--discriminants--principal-subresultants projection first in \(x\) and then in \(s\). Exact rational normalization timed out after fifty-five seconds before the first branch emitted its cleared input list. It consequently produced no explicit projection-polynomial family, no refinement of every full-dimensional true chamber, and no Thom-encoded sample points. This is a failed construction, not evidence that such certificates do not exist. Separate exact checks still verify all five covariance equalities for the rational fork family, positivity of \(T+144/121\) and \(19/4\), the actual-row obstruction \(-2\), and regularity of all eight loading choices at audited points. Those local facts cannot replace the missing global classification.
prose_updates.honest_scope: All covariance-frontier claims remain in the noninjective regime \(2\le p<q\), on the declared theorem-specific generic loci and full-dimensional sign-and-variance chambers. Candidate twins may be variance-neutral, both signs of each true variance change are retained, and no pointwise claim is made on excluded true neutral hyperplanes. The terminal actual-row theorem is exact and independent of variance activity. The fork result is a sound-and-complete regular reduction and an exact projected-union criterion, not an all-chamber feasibility classification. The failed fixed projection attempt is recorded without rerolling to examples, local neighborhoods, or unrestricted quantifier elimination. The node presently named as a bounded-width compiler contributes only the already proved terminal and finite-branch reductions; because \(\omega_p\) is unused, it has no compiler, complexity, or pathwidth force and should be treated as a non-headline supporting proposition. The all-graph realization-or-separator compiler remains only the open-ended question. The prospective workflow may output corrected terminal compatibility and verified individual covariance twins, but not a global high-cumulant information-frontier verdict.

statement_notes.justification: This theorem proves the exact eight-branch projected-union identity, translates frontier membership into the required chamberwise density test, and proves that the rational family plus local regularity cannot decide that test.
statement_notes.gap: The mandated all-true-parameter resultant/subresultant attempt emitted neither the projection family nor Thom-cell certificates, so no chamberwise dense cover or full-dimensional separator has been proved.
statement_notes.consumer: The workflow is prevented from promoting a verified local fork collision into a claim of generic covariance surplus.
